title: Drought pattern under climate change in Harris County, Texas, USA based on CMIP6 projections
abstract: This study assessed future drought conditions in Harris County, Texas, using five Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) General Circulation Models (GCMs) under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios for the period 2026–2085. The analysis employed the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI-6 and SPEI-12) to characterize drought, providing comprehensive insights into future drought risk. The results indicate a substantial increase in drought frequency, intensity, and severity in Harris County, particularly during the far-future period (2056–2085). The study identified an oscillating drought pattern: high frequency (1980–2002), temporary reduction (2003–2024), and projected intensification (2056–2085). Under medium and high emission scenarios, both SPEI-6 and SPEI-12 exhibit significant (p < 0.05) negative trends across the ensemble mean and most individual GCMs for the future period, in contrast to the historical period where both SPEI-6 and SPEI-12 demonstrate slight positive trends. Severity duration frequency curve analysis reveals that future droughts under SPEI-12 will be significantly more severe across all return periods (2–50 years). Although Harris County is experiencing relatively lower drought risk at present, the identified oscillating pattern and projected doubling of drought frequency under SSP5-8.5 represent a critical threshold for regional water security, requiring heightened attention from policymakers for proactive planning and adaptation strategies.
problem: Comprehensive assessments of future drought risk at the county scale are limited, as statewide studies lack local context and no previous research has applied the latest CMIP6 climate projections to evaluate drought patterns specifically for the vulnerable Harris County, Texas region.
method: This study assesses future drought conditions in Harris County, Texas, by employing the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) on five downscaled CMIP6 climate model projections under three emission scenarios for the period 2026-2085.
task: The task is to assess future drought patterns, including frequency, intensity, and severity, in Harris County, Texas, using downscaled CMIP6 climate projections under multiple emission scenarios for the period 2026-2085.
innovation: This paper presents the first comprehensive CMIP6-based drought assessment for Harris County, Texas, identifying a unique three-phase drought pattern and projecting that future long-term drought severity will be five times greater than historical events.

The three-phase temporal pattern we identified likely reflects the interaction between anthropogenic forcing and natural climate variability. The recent reduction in drought frequency (2003-2024) may be influenced by decadal-scale modes of climate variability such as the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO), Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO),El Nino-Southern Oscillation index which modulate regional precipitation patterns (Barlow et al. 2019; Nowbuth 2010; Nielsen-Gammon, 2011).
